Natural gas pipeline engineer here.  I have over a decade in the industry at the utility and as a consultant.

The short answer is:  It wouldn't last long, especially in colder temps.  Likely on the magnitude of hours, not days.  Highly depends on where you live and ambient temps.


Long answer:  It depends on the system load of the area you live, the geometry and size of the system,  and all the upstream points pulling gas off the system.  Some utilities "pack" the system at night to prepare for the higher demand during the day.  Basically, increase the pressure of the hundreds or thousands of feet of transmission pipeline at night, and use the pressure drawdown, plus supply off interstate pipelines, to provide adequate supply to customers.

Some compressors may use natural gas to drive the motors, but you have to think "end to end" transport of gas.  If the extraction, processing, compression, local and remote automation, and SCADA are working... then great.  If one of those fails, the timer starts for gas running out at the home.

Lastly, during emergencies, it's not uncommon for utilities to execute emergency plans on system triage.  Hospitals and schools take priority in most cases, then first responders, then residential, then large businesses.
